teaser: Underwrite and carry the risk in London, sell into the US and EU, raise in one go: £10 million or £50 million, and the cover each buys.
core_idea: An insurer for agent behaviour policies does three jobs, and London suits two of them: a managing agent and Lloyd's coverholder on a syndicate's capital, then its own capital as a UK insurer or at Lloyd's, with distribution into the US through surplus lines and the EU by one registration, and capital raised from investors including the Gulf's funds; because every row is capped, the capital raised above about £4.35 million of running costs sets a ceiling on the cover it can sell, so £10 million in one go backs about £94 million to £188 million and £50 million about £761 million to £1.52 billion.

quotes.text: I think the honest answer is that it can have more than one home, because it does more than one job.
quotes.why: The answer to where, in one line.

quotes.text: So rather than raising in stages, the company can raise once, for the cover it intends to sell from the start, and the size of the raise decides that ceiling.
quotes.why: Why the raise should match the cover from the start.
